propositions: Four dispatch call sites use `cast()` to access optional capability members (`add_comment`, `set_relationship`) without runtime checks, unlike `fetcher.py` which uses `hasattr()` guards.

When a transport lacks an optional capability, `AttributeError` is silently caught by broad `except Exception` handlers, conflating missing-capability (designed skip) with raised-exception (real failure).
Capability-absent conditions must be guarded with `isinstance()` against `@runtime_checkable` Protocols and logged distinctly via the existing `bridge_alerts` channel with capability-specific kinds.

The `_call_with_retry` function must relocate from `dispatch_one.py` (796 LOC, at module size cap) to `dispatch_apply_phases.py` to accommodate new guard statements without exceeding the 800-LOC limit.

Python 3.12+ `@runtime_checkable` uses `getattr_static` which does not detect `__getattr__`-proxied attributes, requiring fallback to `hasattr()` to prevent false-negative capability detection on decorator/wrapper transports.
